correctness.rationale: For every integer d>=1, real alpha>-1 and all positive stretches, Dirichlet(1,...,1,alpha+1) signed-orthant coordinates yield diagonal affine Gram moments and K(x,y)=1+c sum x_i y_i/a_i^2 with c=(m+1)(m+2)/2. The L1 and L∞ norms equal the maximum kernel absolute row sum, attained at and only at vertices by the strictly sign-crossing convexity argument. Exact Beta(1,m) integration gives the stated norm, and strict elementary logarithmic differentiation proves effective-dimension monotonicity. The asymptotic and weak concentration claims follow from explicit expansions/moments. Exact/symbolic/high-precision script checks 204 independent identities/examples, but analytical steps establish universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: Exact sharp uniform-input sensitivity of affine least squares on cross-polytope cells is a natural approximation invariant not supplied by the stronger-sounding metric-projection or simplex references. The theorem covers all dimension and slack Jacobi weights and arbitrary stretches, determines exact maximizing locations, positivity-defect extremizers and dual norms, and proves monotonic dimension-weight dependence with a surprising weak-measure-concentration versus unbounded-norm contrast. It does not claim general higher-degree or other-polytope consequences.
